components.text: The explanatory demand governing contingent members also governs material reality as a whole.
A noncircular explanation beyond contingent reality is preferable to an ultimate brute fact.
Challenges extending ordinary explanatory expectations to total material reality.
Ordinary explanatory intuitions may fail when extended to material reality as a whole.
Reframes the issue from maximal certainty to weaker automatic actuality.
A foundational layer can be classified as automatically actual under a weaker sense of necessity.
The explanatory demand on contingent things reaches the universe even at its first temporal boundary.
Challenges applying causal-explanatory intuitions at time's first boundary.
Allows contingency while denying that a temporal beginning requires an external cause.
Explanatory reasoning grounded in experienced reality lacks warrant at the ultimate temporal boundary.
Ordinary explanatory practice need not extend to total material reality.
Defends continuity between ordinary or scientific reasoning and ultimate inquiry.
Opposes abandoning explanatory inquiry at the level of total reality.
An available necessary explanation should satisfy explanatory inquiry better than brute reality.
Automatic actuality supplies an explanatory foundation rather than a modal redescription.
A weaker sense of necessity provides explanatory value once attributed to a foundation.
Diagnoses necessity as a conditional label rather than an existence explanation.
Challenges automatic actuality as an explanatory terminus rather than mere redescription.
Argues that weakening necessity does not explain why the foundation exists.
Necessary existence does not explain why the proposed foundation is actual.
A brute contingent universe may stand without the ordinary further-explanation demand.
Distinguishes contrastive explanatory demand from continued curiosity about actuality.
Offers a non-temporal modal basis for why explanation is especially demanded.
Grounds inquiry in could-have-failed actuality rather than merely local causal intuition.
A supreme nature may explain or predict why the foundation is robustly automatically actual.
Diagnoses a backward explanation between divine supremacy and necessary existence.
Supremacy cannot explain necessity if necessity partly constitutes supremacy.
Necessary existence leaves the foundation's actuality unexplained.
Answers that no further explanation is required once necessary actuality is reached.
Abandons reliance on supremacy by locating termination directly in inability not to exist.
Necessary existence is no more explanatory than brute existence.
The universe may remain brute at the ultimate boundary.
Total material reality may be brute despite ordinary explanatory practice.
Compares the residual demands generated by brute contingency and brute necessity.
Argues that modal contingency remains explanation-demanding even at an ultimate boundary.
Rejects parity between brute total reality and automatic actuality.
Sets divine supremacy aside and bases the comparison on modality.
Modal contingency makes an ultimate entity explanatorily dependent in a way necessity does not.
A noncontingent foundation follows from explanatory independence.
Diagnoses a conflation of modal contingency with causal dependence.
Challenges the inference from foundational independence to existence in every world.
Clarifies that weak modal nonnecessity need not imply dependence.
Logical necessity supplies an intelligible model for the necessary structure of foundational reality.
A concrete automatically actual foundation is supported by the character of necessary reality.
Challenges any move from logical necessity to ontological grounding.
Distinguishes inferential rules from a necessary concrete reality.
Logical content may be only a feature of language and statements rather than mind-independent reality.
Independence can be separated from necessary existence.
Answers by distinguishing mind-independent content from its representations.
Proposes a unified necessary nature rather than inferring dependence from modality.
A concrete necessary foundation can inherit or include the necessity of an abstract landscape.
A weaker necessity avoids the demand for an evident contradiction in divine nonexistence.
Identifies the missing analogue between abstract and concrete necessity.
Notes that even weaker necessity needs an intelligible basis for concrete application.
The apparent coherence of divine nonexistence supports its metaphysical possibility.
Possible-world nonexistence can be separated from dependence.
Challenges the inference from apparent noncontradiction to genuine possibility.
Questions whether conceivable nonexistence establishes modal contingency.
Uses inferentially extended contradiction rather than bare linguistic appearance.
A foundation outside the contingent plurality must therefore be noncontingent or necessary.
An explanation not among the contingent things explained must itself be noncontingent.
Conceivability limitations supply positive warrant for necessary existence.
Identifies the unsupported leap from foundational status to necessity.
Accepts explanatory bottoming out without granting existence in every possible world.
Distinguishes mere conceivability from the still-missing positive necessity inference.
Brute necessity is explanatorily superior to brute contingency because only contingency calls for explanation.
Automatic actuality answers the relevant why-question about the foundation.
Necessary existence supplies a uniquely legitimate stopping point.
Challenges the claimed explanatory advantage of brute necessity over brute contingency.
Argues that stopping at God supplies no explanation unavailable to the universe.
Rejects necessary existence as helping explain why God exists.
Preserves a brute-universe alternative to the proposed necessary foundation.
Necessary existence offers no explanatory advantage over a brute universe.
No coherent model connects abstract necessity to a concrete foundation.
Logical structure cannot ground concrete causal reality.
Offers an immaterial conceptual mind as a coherent concrete model.
Locates abstract structure within the nature of a causally powerful mind.
Shows coherence of immaterial concreteness but not necessary existence.
Distinguishes God from material reality through conceptuality and causal powers.
